deals.evidence: King Power, run by the Srivaddhanaprabha family, bought Leicester for £35m from Milan Mandaric in 2010.
deals.headline: King Power buys Leicester City from Milan Mandaric
deals.investor: King Power (Srivaddhanaprabha family), as Asian Football Investments
deals.summary: A Thai-led consortium, Asian Football Investments, fronted by King Power's Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha, took over the club in 2010; Sky Sports reports the price as £35m. Before the brief's 2015 window but the transaction behind the current ownership.

deals.evidence: e) Macquarie Bank Limited: £50,000,000 secured on Premier League receivables of
deals.headline: Macquarie lends Leicester £50m against Premier League receivables
deals.source_name: Leicester City FC annual report 2024/25, note 12
deals.summary: A £50m Macquarie Bank loan secured on Premier League receivables, at 8.30%, repayable in instalments to March 2027 (£49.7m unpaid at 30 June 2025). Macquarie also provides transfer-fee receivable discounting facilities (four further loans of £7.4m-£20.8m at 6.80%-9.02%) and a £10m facility secured on future receivables.

deals.evidence: following the conversion of £124.0m of group loans converted to equity
deals.headline: Owner converts £124m of loans into equity
deals.summary: Loans of £124.0m from the group were converted into equity in 2024/25, lowering interest owed to group undertakings; the parent also lent £14.3m of new working-capital loans in the year and, after year end, five-year facilities totalling £28m.

deals.evidence: The project is titled "Project Lineup" and values the physical assets at £224m with no specific sum placed on the sale of King Power's football teams.
deals.headline: King Power puts Leicester City up for sale through Citi
deals.summary: Sky Sports saw a Citi sales brochure ('Project Lineup') offering the men's and women's teams, King Power Stadium, both training facilities and sister club OH Leuven; it values the physical assets at £224m with no specific sum placed on the teams. Citi forecasts 2026 financial-year revenue of £97m. Not a completed transaction.

founded_evidence: Formed in 1884, Leicester City Football Club, formerly known as Leicester Fosse until 1919
name: Leicester City Football Club
notes: League: relegated from the Championship at the end of 2025/26 (six-point PSR deduction) and plays in EFL League One in 2026/27 (NBC Connecticut, 21 Apr 2026; the club's kit release speaks of 'an immediate return to the EFL Championship'); league field kept as given for the key. Accounts are to 30 June 2025 (2024/25, a Premier League season); 2025/26 accounts not yet filed. Revenue split as the club gives it: broadcasting £117.4m, sponsorship and advertising £37.3m, gate receipts £20.3m, commercial £9.3m, other £2.2m - commercial left null because the club reports sponsorship separately and nothing may be summed. Ownership stake: PSC register says 75% or more; the club says the family are sole owners - no exact percentage stated, so stake_pct is null. No valuation published (Citi's brochure values physical assets only, at £224m). Liu Shilai is a vice-chairman and director since 2012; no page states him as a shareholder. No social follower counts found on a citable page.
